rationale: B is materially more useful because it gives a concrete near-term path: analyze incidents for 1–2 weeks, then do targeted hardening over one sprint to six weeks, possibly rewriting only failing subsystems. It also explains why full auth rewrites are unusually risky and why the current system’s accumulated knowledge matters. A names a plausible strategy (strangler migration) but provides little discriminative reasoning, weak caveats, no clear alternative framing, and almost no actionable next steps beyond a vague migration pattern. Neither has strong quantitative support, but B’s time-boxed steps are more decision-relevant.
